oracle.ref: PR #1100 (fix); fix evidence: Local stand 09/10/2026, uiweekwp.tracy.test: turn session-5e3bc0e7…:1 closed_at 18:22:21.223 (= the host's end of moment job 32a6ced4ff6d) while turn :2 opened at 18:22:00.995; same pattern for session-2c77b352… (tasks/evidence/followups-2026-10-10/p5-turns/overlap-uiweekwp.txt).
oracle.invariant: S1 exits 0 and every test in run.tests reports ok, none skipped (the database was really used). The stand's sequence through the dsh's own turn book: turn 1's /moment answers 202 with its moment running, turn 2 opens, turn 2's first write is still held 150 ms later and is let go only after turn 1's moment ended on the host (p5-timing writeReleased >= moment1Ended). Records after it: turn 1 closed_at (the host's end of its moment) <= turn 2's first write; turn 1 head is turn 1's commit, turn 2 head is turn 2's commit; turn 1 concurrent = false and turn 2 unsealed_start = false. When turn 1's moment ended inside its own door's wait, POST /turn names no momentsPending, tracy-web is not asked, and turn 2's first write waits under 5 ms (p5-no-wait). POST /api/sites/:key/moment/wait answers {ended:false} while the host commits and {ended:true} once it has, with turn 1 closed under its commit by the wait itself; a malformed turn id is 400. At the bound: release answers {released:true}; if the moment then commits, turn 1 is marked concurrent and turn 2 unsealed_start; if it commits nothing, nothing is marked. The dsh's own bound test lets the write go after ~60 ms and sends exactly one release. The open carries waitsForMoments: true; a dsh that does not send it hears the moment named but its seal does not take that moment as harmless.
